quotes.text: Action based message extensions break that snarl of interruptions by letting you stay exactly where the conversation is happening. You don't have to jump between windows or remember a list of trigger phrases.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the core benefit of action-based extensions over bots and tabs.

quotes.text: The manifest file is the contract that tells teams where your back end lives, what permissions you need, and how the extension should display.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Adaptive cards bring structure, sections, buttons, bold highlights, even embedded images, and let users interact without ever leaving teams.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

takeaways: Bots and tabs get most of the attention, but message extensions remove context switching by bringing live data straight into Teams conversations.
Search extensions surface records, action extensions collect input and trigger back-end processes, and link unfurling turns pasted URLs into rich previews.
A precise app manifest, tightly scoped permissions, staged rollouts and compliance checks decide whether an extension scales across the organization.
hook: Fetching a sales record or ticket during a Teams chat often means five clicks and a lost conversation. This episode is for Teams developers and admins who want custom apps people actually use. You will learn when to use bots, tabs or message extensions, how to build an action-based extension with Adaptive Cards, and how to deploy it safely.
